To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the expression levels and the expression ratios of chaperones should be optimized for the maximum biotransformative activities in whole‐cell catalysts.
the expression levels for chaperones should be optimized to achieve high biotransformation efficiency in whole‐cell systems.

the archaeal γ‐prefoldins and thermosomes can be used as chaperones to enhance the activity of recombinantly expressed enzymes, and that the degree of activity enhancement is dependent on the expression level of chaperones.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the biotransformation of ricinoleic acid into γ‐lactone by recombinant Esch. coli expressing the alcohol dehydrogenases (ADHs) from M. luteus and the Baeyer–Villerger monooxygenase (BVMO) from Pseudomonas sp. KT
the development of a whole‐cell bioreactor system for biotransformation.
the use of recombinant microorganisms for the production of biologically derived compounds, such as pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals and industrial chemicals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the expression of the archaeal chapers (i.e. γ‐prefoldins and thermosomes) in recombinant Escheichia coli expressing M. luteus ADH and the P. putida Baeyer‐Villiger monoxigenase improved the biotransformation of ricinoleic acid significantly.

the expression levels and the expression of chaperones are crucial factors to achieve high‐level biotransformation activities in recombinant E. coli expressing M. luteus ADH and P. putida Baeyer−Villiger monoxidase.
the expression levels and the activity of chaperone proteins are crucial for the stability of the enzymes and, therefore, for the biotransformation efficiency of whole‐cell bioreactors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the chaperones from archaea, which are thermophiles or hyperthermophiles, can stabilize the activity of recombinants of E. coli.
the expression levels and the expression of chaperones in recombinant E. coli can be optimized to achieve the maximum biotransfomation activity of the recombinant enzymes.
the expression levels for chaperones should be optimized to achieve the maximum biotransformations activity in the whole‐cell bioreactor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression levels for chaperone co‐expression must be optimized to obtain maximum biotransformations activity in whole‐cells.
chaperones can be utilized as a tool to improve the biotransformation activities of whole‐cell bioprocesses.
we demonstrated for the first of time that the archaea chaperones (γ‐prefoldin) can stabilize enzyme activities in vivo.
